verbatim_user_utterance: Next task, devise a wrapper to contain the account custom instruction as either individual rules or group rules on a subject..where the grouped rules a presented in an array, where the first index clarifies the scope of the other indices and one subject is allowed per array. And the ungrouped indices are rules adopted in an adhoc manner and typically appended from newest to oldest and where the last index of the array gives any rules or instructions for interpretation of the array

task.objective: Devise a machine-readable wrapper representation for the account custom instruction that can accommodate individual ad hoc rules and subject-specific grouped rules.

requirements.requirement: Represent account custom instructions as one outer JSON array with a permanently pinned explainer object at index 0.

Store the structural rules template separately at references/rules-template.json and refer to it through the outer explainer's rules_template_path member, rather than defining the template inside itself.
Store machine-dialect writing rules and examples separately at references/machine-dialect-rules.json and refer to them through the outer explainer's machine_dialect_rules_path member.
Use self-describing, context-complete machine dialect in every explainer, standalone rule, group rule, and nested instructional member; valid JSON by itself is insufficient.
Allow verbose multi-member explainer and rule objects where their context, conditions, and relationships require it; avoid undefined, artificial pseudo-machine brevity.
Make each standalone rule one complete object occupying exactly one parent-array index and including a descriptive title, however many nested models, requirements, and examples the rule contains.
Represent each subject-specific group as one nested array occupying one index of its parent, containing only one subject and a titled index-zero group explainer.
Keep the explainer of every outer and nested array pinned at index 0 throughout changes.
Insert newly adopted outer entries at index 1, shifting older entries without changing their contents or relative order.
Insert newly adopted entries within an inner group at index 1, preserving its pinned explainer and existing entry order.
Apply explicit local interpretation overrides only within the group where defined and preserve all nonconflicting inherited instructions.
Preserve substantive rule requirements; when inserting the accepted user scope rule add only its title, leaving its applicability, model, and ten examples identical.
Provide an instantiated wrapper draft containing the accepted user scope rule as one outer rule object and a nested conversation-analytics group without falsely asserting activation.

task.deliverable: Wrapper draft with title, applicability and standalone_rule_path for User-Defined Scope, and analogous referenced Conversation Analytics rule, plus external rule standards and equivalent aliased copy.
acceptance_criteria: An outer array exists with index-zero explainer referencing both rule-set paths; no self-redefinition of template structure is embedded there.
Every nested group has a titled index-zero explainer identifying its single subject.
Complete standalone rules are represented as whole titled objects occupying one array index.
New entries are inserted at index 1 while array explainers stay at index 0.
Both reference files define contextual machine-readable requirements and concrete examples.
The accepted scope rule's applicability, model, and ten examples are unchanged.
The analytics rule body is semantically intact and not represented as operationally activated.
The revision draft remains pending user acceptance, with the previously rejected artifacts preserved.

resolved_design_decisions.decision: The explainer is pinned at index 0 in all instruction arrays; former final-index explainer semantics are superseded.
New outer and inner entries are inserted at index 1; indices of existing entries shift without changing contents or order.
Every standalone rule is a single complete object with a title; a group is one nested array whose index-zero explainer contains a group title.
Rules and explainers use semantically complete, contextual machine dialect; pseudo-machine shorthand without defined meaning is unacceptable.
The array structural rules and the rule-writing rules are separate referenced documents with examples, not copied into the outer index-zero explainer.

amendments.verbatim_user_utterance: The newest rule should be appended to the beginning of the array and all indices renumbered accordingly...the nested elements should follow the rules of their local index when they override the outer scope
amendments.purpose: Resolve ordering and nested interpretation precedence questions without altering the original task request.
Apply latest user revisions to the wrapper design without treating the design as accepted before review.
amendments.user_instruction_summary: Store detailed structural rules and examples in a separate Terminals references rules template; store a second reference document for machine-dialect writing requirements and examples; reference both from the wrapper's index-zero explainer, preserving the accepted verbose user scope rule as one titled object.

amendments.purpose: Make Conversation Analytics one standalone rule object because the former two-element grouped-rule array added only redundant context.
amendments.user_instruction_summary: Conversation analytics should be an object, not an array. Its former group-explainer at index 0 and the subordinate rule at index 1 were redundant; retain one complete analytics rule object without the superfluous group explainer.
amendments.implementation: Replace outer index 2 with the preexisting complete titled analytics rule object, preserving its original rule body byte-for-byte at the parsed JSON value level. Update the editable aliased copy and its exact-key alias lookup without modifying the separate accepted analytics source.

amendments.purpose: Externalize verbose Conversation Analytics details and expose the referenced rule, conversation template, and destination directly on one outer-array entry.
amendments.user_instruction_summary: Create a revised Conversation Analytics rule that renames rule to applicability and includes explicit keys for the location of the standalone rule, conversation template path, and destination.
amendments.implementation: In the wrapper, replace outer index 2 with a titled object containing applicability, standalone_rule_path, conversation_template_path, and destination. In the standalone reference, rename the rule member to applicability while preserving its exact value and all remaining members. Refresh the alias copy and dictionary. Preserve the accepted source document as historical.

amendments.purpose: Shorten outer index-one scope instruction without changing the complete standalone rule.
amendments.user_instruction_summary: Keep title and applicability; remove all other members from the embedded rule and add a path to the standalone scope reference.
amendments.implementation: Outer index 1 now contains title, applicability, and standalone_rule_path only. The complete model and ten examples remain in references/user-defined-scope-rule.json. The aliased copy and lookup are synchronized.

amendments.purpose: Add an explicit repository-documentation preflight instruction to the outer index-zero explainer.
amendments.user_instruction_summary: Before carrying out operations in a GitHub repository, fetch and read its README and AGENTS documents, using Markdown or JSON variants. Express the instruction equivalently rather than verbatim.
amendments.implementation: The outer index-zero explainer has a github_repository_documentation_preflight instruction. Update the aliased copy and the alias reference without modifying the complete standalone scope and analytics rules.

amendments.purpose: Make relative instruction reference paths independently resolvable to an identified GitHub repository and branch.
amendments.user_instruction_summary: The relative paths are ambiguous without a base storage location; specify the source repository, branch, and a direct retrieval mechanism in the wrapper.
amendments.implementation: Add reference_base_url and reference_resolution to outer index zero. Keep reference_base_url and alias_lookup_path literal in the aliased copy so the alias map can be retrieved before decoding. Preserve all existing rule entries and relative paths.

previous_requirements_before_current_rev.requirement: Support both standalone individual rules and grouped rules organized by subject.
Represent each subject group as an array.
Use the first element (index 0) of each grouped-rule array to clarify the scope governing its remaining elements.
Allow exactly one subject per grouped-rule array; do not combine unrelated subjects in the same group.

Represent ad hoc standalone rules in newest-to-oldest order. Insert each new ad hoc rule at index 0 of its applicable ad hoc rule array, shifting all existing elements one position forward and renumbering their array indices accordingly.
Reserve the final element of each array that defines interpretation instructions for the interpretation rules applicable to that array; its index changes when new elements are inserted ahead of it.

Interpret nested/grouped arrays using their local index rules; where local rules explicitly override outer-scope interpretation, local rules take precedence within that nested array. Preserve group index 0 as its single-subject scope definition and its final element as its local interpretation instructions.
Preserve the content and behavioral scope of existing account custom instructions; wrapper design must not silently change their meanings.

context.related_prior_task_objective: Condense the existing account scope instruction into a minimally verbose machine instruction without loss of intended meaning.
context.relation: This task specifies a containing structure for account custom instructions and is distinct from editing or activating those instructions.

rejection.reason: User explicitly rejected the submitted design artifact; no specific replacement criteria supplied.
